event_text: A Macedonian army led by Philip II defeated the combined forces of Athens and Thebes in the Battle of Chaeronea, securing Macedonian hegemony in Greece and the Aegean.
headline: Philip II of Macedon Conquers Greece at Chaeronea
story: Barry gazed out at the ancient battlefield, where the Athenians and Thebans were attempting to halt the Macedonian advance. 'Susan, it's 338 BCE, and Philip II is about to secure his legacy. His son Alexander is just a teenager, but he's already learning the family business – conquering one's neighbours.' Susan pecked at a stray seed, 'The Athenians, under Demosthenes, thought they could take on the Macedonians with their fancy phalanx formation. But Philip's been modernizing his army, and those long pikes are proving rather... persuasive.' Barry snorted, 'Persuasive? The Macedonians are rolling over the Athenian lines like they're, well, not exactly an unstoppable force, but more like a mildly irritated one. The Thebans are putting up a bit more of a fight, but it's not looking good for them.' Susan adjusted her wing, 'The consequences will be far-reaching, I suppose. Macedonian dominance, the end of Greek city-state independence... and, of course, the eventual rise of Alexander the Great. One wonders what the Greeks will make of it all.' Barry shrugged, 'Probably the same thing they make of most defeats – a stirring speech, a tragic play, and a few choice curses for the victors.'
regret_line: Rather a shame they didn't take that whole "city-state independence" thing more seriously, in hindsight.
winner_line: The concept of imperialism, it seems, was the real victor that day.
